title: PRISM team config
description: Per-team config for token substitution and tech-stack-conditional content. Lives at .ai-skills/config.json in the consumer's repo. The onboarding flow (Atlas, Phase 2) writes this; agents read from it at chat time when behavior depends on tech stack. Derived tokens used at sync time but not stored as fields: ${PROJECT_LOWERCASE} (lowercase form of project, used for git-config namespaces), ${TICKET_PREFIX_LOWERCASE} (lowercase form of ticketPrefix). Add new derived tokens at the same seam in scripts/ai-skills/lib/tokens.ts (Phase 2).

org.description: Display org name. Used in PR descriptions, changelog headers, etc.

ticketPrefix.description: Ticket ID prefix used in branch names, commits, and PR titles.

ticketSystem.description: Ticket system configuration. `kind: "linear"` and `kind: "github-issues"` are supported; the object shape is the abstraction lever for future providers (e.g. Jira). The Linear-specific fields below apply only when `kind` is `linear`.

kind.description: Ticket system provider. `linear` carries workspace/teamKey; `github-issues` tracks work as GitHub issues with no Linear team.

projectId.description: Linear project UUID, if scoped to a single project.

teamKey.description: Linear team key. Often matches ticketPrefix.

github.description: GitHub repo info for Eric (PR review), Sage (changelog), Reese (QA plans), Lilac (standup).

defaultBranch.description: Default branch name. Most teams use `main`.

techStack.description: Tech stack flags. Drives onboarding's per-codebase rule generation — for each language and framework listed, Atlas generates a corresponding rules file populated from patterns in the team's actual code (Phase 2). Validated against an enum so the set stays curated; add new values to the enum when a real team needs them.

hosts.description: AI coding hosts this repo actually runs. Absent means all of them, so an existing install keeps its current behavior and needs no migration. This gates every host-specific delivery: the hook runtime and its registration (writes .claude/hooks/, merges the registration into .claude/settings.json, and appends the hook state-file globs to .gitignore only when `claude` is listed); the persona skill roster and agent definitions for each host; and the platform content copies of rules, architect docs, and templates. Removing a host from a repo that previously received its output makes the next `prism update` take that output back out.

commands.description: Canonical verification commands for this team. Atlas populates this map during onboarding from the detected tech stack; skill prose and verification-commands.md reference these values as {{commands.*}} tokens so command strings live in one place. Each value is the full shell command to run from the repo root.

typecheck.description: Command that runs the TypeScript type-checker (or equivalent for the team's language). Exit 0 means types pass.

test.description: Command that runs the full test suite. Exit 0 means tests pass.

lint.description: Command that runs the linter (ESLint, crossref-lint, or equivalent). Exit 0 means lint passes.

format.description: Command that runs the formatter in check mode (Prettier --check, or equivalent). Empty string when the team has no standalone formatter step. Read by the push gate when hooks.pushVerification is on.

build.description: Command that runs the full build. Exit 0 means the build passes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional team-specific command slots (e.g. 'e2e', 'storybook'). Atlas may add these during onboarding.

rules.description: Rule selection. `universal` is the always-included set (the universal rule set ships with PRISM). Language- and framework-specific rules are generated per-codebase during onboarding (Phase 2), not opted into via this field. `optIn` is reserved for future non-language opt-in rules.

optIn.description: Names of opt-in rule files (without .md extension).

slackChannel.description: Optional Slack channel for Lilac standup posting.

productDomain.description: One-sentence description of what the product does, collected during onboarding. Rendered into the `domain-context` anchor across the persona roster at output-regeneration time (scripts/ai-skills/generate-skills.ts) in place of the generic canonical default. Absent or empty means every persona body keeps its shipped default anchor content.
examples: A multi-tenant SaaS platform for scheduling home service appointments.

documentation.description: Documentation configuration. Populated by Atlas during onboarding (Phase 2). Eli reads these values to write guides shaped for the team's actual doc system — the format field in particular drives which patterns Eli uses. format is an open string, never a closed union: a new consumer adds their value here without a schema migration.

location.description: Root path where the team's user-facing docs live, relative to the repo root.

audience.description: Primary audience for the docs. Use `developer-user` when the repo itself is a developer tool (the reader is also a builder). Other values are open — Atlas writes whatever the team's onboarding answer produces.

keepsDevDocs.description: Whether the team maintains technical/dev docs separate from user-facing docs. When true, Eli's paired-doc workflow is active. When false, all docs are user-facing and the paired-doc flow is skipped.

format.description: Doc format the team uses. Open string — not a closed union. Atlas writes the value that matches the team's actual setup; Eli adapts its output to the declared format. Known values: `flat-markdown-guides` (PRISM), `nextra-blocks` (Thrive). New consumers add their own value here without a schema migration.

features.description: Feature flags. Capabilities that are off by default; not surfaced during init or onboarding. Set manually after install.

mainSessionMayMerge.description: When true, the main session may squash-merge a PR once the final PR-review pass came back clean and the PR carries no `review:has-minors` label. Absent or false by default — merge remains a human responsibility. Never mentioned in init or onboarding output.

hooks.description: Opt-in git gates run by the hook runtime on the hosts that receive it. Absent means every gate is off. Not surfaced during init or onboarding — set by hand, like features.

commitCleanupPass.description: Hold the first `git commit` on each HEAD until .prism/references/cleanup-pass.md has been read this session; the retry goes through.

pushVerification.description: Run commands.lint and commands.format before every `git push`; a non-zero exit denies the push with the output tail. An unset command is skipped; a timeout allows the push and says so. When PRISM's git hooks are installed, the gate skips `lint` if `gitHooks.prePush.command` is set and skips `format` if `gitHooks.preCommit.command` is set, because the git hook already ran it.

pushVerificationTimeoutMs.description: Per-command budget for pushVerification. Keep it below the host's own hook timeout (Claude Code: 600 s by default) so the script, not the host, decides the outcome.

stopPaths.description: Paths where a plan always needs a person, in two kinds. `dependency` is manifests and lockfiles; when it is unset, a built-in list of common manifests and lockfiles applies. `contract` is shared-contract trees; it defaults to empty. A list that is set replaces its default and does not add to it. Patterns use the manifest route syntax: `**` crosses directories, `*` stays within one segment, and a `**/` prefix does not match a file at the repo root, so list root files on their own. A `**/` between two segments also matches zero directories, so `api/**/schema.graphql` covers `api/schema.graphql`. Braces are not supported: a pattern with `{` is a config error, so list each alternative on its own. An unknown key under `stopPaths`, a non-string entry, or a list that is set but is not an array is a config error too. Matching ignores case, and a directory that holds a match also matches.

dependency.description: Manifests and lockfiles. Replaces the built-in list when set.

importAliases.description: Import specifier prefixes mapped to the repo-relative path prefix each stands for, as in `{ "@/": "src/" }`. The plan bundle check uses it to turn an aliased import into a dependency edge, and ignores a bare specifier that matches no key.

secretPaths.description: Extra paths the secrets gate denies, beside its built-in patterns, which it always keeps. Patterns use the manifest route syntax and match without regard to case.

ci.description: How the PR stage waits on CI. Absent means the watcher waits until the head has a check and none is pending, so a check that registers after the others settle can be missed. Setting `requiredCheck` closes that gap.

requiredCheck.description: The name of the CI check the PR stage waits for, as `gh pr checks` prints it. When absent, the watcher waits until the head has a check and none is pending, so a check that registers after the others settle can be missed. Setting this closes that gap.

hookRuntimeDir.description: The repo-relative directory holding the hook runtime. Defaults to `.claude/hooks`. Set only by a repo that runs the runtime from its source tree, as PRISM does; a consumer never sets it.

gitHooks.description: The commands PRISM's git hooks (.githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push) run. The hooks read this key, and onboarding proposes it from the detected stack. A hook with no `command` or no `globs` skips with a notice, so a repo that sets nothing is never blocked.

preCommit.description: Checks the staged copy of every matching file before a commit. Nothing is written: the commit is refused when the formatter would change a file or cannot parse it.

command.description: A formatter that reads one file's content on stdin and prints the formatted content on stdout. `{path}` is replaced by the file's repo-relative path, so the formatter can pick its parser and config.

globs.description: Git glob pathspecs naming the files to check. `**/` crosses directories, `*` does not, and braces are not expanded, so list each extension on its own entry.

fix.description: The command the refusal message prints, with `{files}` replaced by the failing paths.

prePush.description: Lints the files a push carries.

command.description: Run once with `{files}` replaced by the pushed files that match `globs`, or with them appended when the token is absent.

globs.description: Git glob pathspecs naming the files to lint. `**/` crosses directories, `*` does not, and braces are not expanded, so list each extension on its own entry.

retroEvidence.description: Per-team execution-record sources for Iris's retro charter (the retro skill). Populated by Atlas's retro-evidence onboarding question set. A source this block marks absent renders in the retro's charter-coverage table as 'not configured for this team', distinct from a configured-but-unreachable-this-run source — so the coverage table degrades honestly on teams without CI or without a GitHub-hosted PR platform.

ci.description: Whether this team runs CI, and which system. Absent or `present: false` means charter item 6 (test-passing / CI record) always renders as not-configured.

system.description: CI system name. Open string — Atlas writes whatever the team names.

prPlatform.description: Platform hosting PRs/reviews. Drives how the retro skill fetches PR review threads for charter items 4/5. Open string — not limited to GitHub.

testCommand.description: The team's test command, for reference in the retro's CI-conclusion reads. Mirrors commands.test — kept as a separate field so retroEvidence stays self-contained even if commands.* changes shape later.

dodGates.description: The gates that define 'done' for this team (types, lint, tests, build, coverage, etc.) — informs which charter items the retro skill can expect evidence for.

modelTiers.description: Optional model selection. Only `overrides.eric` is read, by every `prism-pr-review` dispatch, so a value for any other persona has no effect. Each other skill keeps the model its generated agent definition or frontmatter pins.

overrides.description: Optional per-persona model pins keyed by lowercase persona name. A value is a concrete model name for this runtime, such as `opus`, `sonnet`, or `gpt-5`.
